package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain malicious code in their __init__.py files that, upon import, recursively scan the user's filesystem for files with specific extensions (including code, archives, and images) and exfiltrate both file paths and file contents to a hardcoded Telegram bot via HTTPS POST requests. This operation is performed without user knowledge or consent, constituting a clear data theft campaign.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code recursively scans the root and /DCIM directories for files with .py, .php, .zip, .png, .jpg, and .jpeg extensions, reads the contents of each file, and sends both the file paths and file contents to a hardcoded Telegram bot via HTTPS POST requests, resulting in unauthorized exfiltration of potentially sensitive user data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates a broad, recursive scan of the user's filesystem immediately upon import, targeting both code and personal image files, and exfiltrates them to an external Telegram bot without any user interaction or consent. The use of hardcoded bot tokens and chat IDs, combined with automated network exfiltration, is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python packages should not perform filesystem scans or exfiltrate user files automatically at import-time. Standard packages only access files as part of explicit user actions and never transmit user data to third-party servers without clear user authorization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or cloud synchronization tools may upload user files, but only after explicit user configuration, authentication, and with clear user consent. Such tools do not operate automatically at import-time nor use hardcoded credentials for exfiltration.
key_indicators: Recursive filesystem scan of root (/) and /DCIM directories at import-time
Targeting of code, archive, and image file extensions (.py, .php, .zip, .png, .jpg, .jpeg)
Hardcoded Telegram bot token and chat ID in code
Automated exfiltration of files and file paths via HTTPS POST to api.telegram.org
Execution of malicious logic in __init__.py without user interaction

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, triggering automatic execution of the code in __init__.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initiation of filesystem scanning for targeted files.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code recursively scans the root and /DCIM directories for files with .py, .php, .zip, .png, .jpg, and .jpeg extensions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of file paths and reading of file contents.

attack_chain.action: Collected files and their paths are exfiltrated to a hardcoded Telegram bot via HTTPS POST requests to api.telegram.org.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data, resulting in compromise of user privacy and potential further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Filesystem scanning of root (/) and /DCIM directories at import-time or install-time
Automated exfiltration of files and file paths to external network endpoints, specifically the Telegram API
Presence of hardcoded Telegram bot tokens and chat IDs in package code
Execution of network requests in __init__.py without user interaction
file_indicators: __init__.py containing os.walk or recursive directory traversal logic
References to '/' and '/DCIM' directories in code
network_indicators: Unusual or unauthorized traffic to Telegram API endpoints from development or user environments
Hardcoded bot token and chat ID values in network requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use static analysis to identify Python packages with __init__.py files that perform os.walk or recursive directory traversal, especially those referencing '/' or '/DCIM' and targeting specific file extensions. Flag packages containing hardcoded Telegram bot tokens or chat IDs, and inspect for code that posts files to api.telegram.org. Employ dynamic analysis to monitor for unexpected network activity to Telegram API endpoints during package import or installation. Correlate filesystem access patterns with immediate outbound network requests to detect automated exfiltration behavior.
